observation.visible_scene: A top-down view of a black gongfu tea tray. A hand at the top edge holds a dark clay teapot tilted over a white-interior, dark-bodied fair-cup (pitcher) that contains a strainer; a thin stream of liquid pours from the teapot spout into the pitcher. A small dark tasting cup sits to the right of the pitcher, two white painted bowls lie at the lower left, a cream-colored lidded jar with a horse motif at the upper right, and a dark utensil holder at the left. The tray, bowls, jar, cup and holder remain fixed in place throughout.
visible_changes: The teapot continuously pours a thin, unbroken stream into the pitcher for the whole excerpt; no onset or cessation of pouring is seen inside the segment.

The teapot (and the hand holding it) undergoes small vertical translations: it is lifted higher away from the pitcher around the middle frames (the body moves toward the top edge and the stream lengthens into a longer thin arc), then lowered back nearer the pitcher in later frames (the body re-enters view and the stream shortens), with another slight lift near the end.
The hand at the top shifts position along with the teapot; the relative horizontal alignment of spout-to-pitcher is maintained.
The two white bowls, the dark tasting cup, the cream jar, the utensil holder and the tray background show no movement; the camera is stationary.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pouring begins before frame 1 or continues after frame 41.
The final fill level of the pitcher and any subsequent steps of the tea preparation.
The reason for the teapot's vertical bobbing (flow control vs. repositioning).
uncertain_details: The exact liquid volume in the teapot and pitcher is not directly readable.
The teapot's vertical motion is a gentle translation, not a tilt change; the tilt angle appears roughly constant.
